skill.name: web-design-guidelines
skill.description: Review web interface files against Vercel-style design, accessibility, and UX guidelines.
skill.summary: Review UI files for Web Interface Guidelines compliance and concise file-line findings.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: The markdown backtick detections are false positives: they are inline formatting and a fenced URL block. The hardcoded WebFetch URL is confirmed as a low network risk, and the larger concern is reliance on mutable remote content as instructions.

remediation.issue: Mutable remote guidelines are treated as instructions
remediation.suggestion: Pin the URL to a reviewed commit or vendor the guidelines into the skill package, then update through marketplace review.

remediation.issue: Network fetch is required for each review
remediation.suggestion: Document the outbound request and ask before fetching, or provide an offline fallback for users who block network access.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

finding_verdicts.reason: The snippet is inline Markdown showing the requested file:line output format. It is not evaluated as code and does not execute a Ruby or shell command.
The snippet is a fenced code block delimiter surrounding a URL. It is Markdown formatting, not Ruby backtick execution or shell invocation.
The skill instructs the agent to fetch a hardcoded raw GitHub URL before reviews. This intended network dependency can pull changed remote content and should be disclosed and controlled.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Instruction Supply Chain
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md directs the agent to fetch remote guidelines and says the fetched content contains all rules and output format instructions. Treating mutable network content as instructions can change skill behavior after marketplace review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly requires fetching the URL and following rules from fetched content; the risk depends on future remote content but the delegation pattern is clear.

content.user_title: Review Web Interfaces Against Design Guidelines
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent UI, accessibility, and UX checks before release. This skill applies Web Interface Guidelines to selected files and reports concise findings.
actual_capabilities: Fetches current Web Interface Guidelines from the configured source.
Reviews user-selected files or asks for a file pattern.
Checks interface code against design, accessibility, and UX rules.
Reports issues with concise file and line references.
Supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code review workflows.
limitations: Requires network access to fetch the latest external guidelines.
Does not apply code changes unless the user requests edits.
Review quality depends on the files supplied by the user.
Does not replace manual usability research or visual QA.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge UI Review
use_cases.description: Check component and page files for guideline issues before opening or merging a pull request.

use_cases.title: Design QA Support
use_cases.description: Compare implemented screens with interface quality expectations and accessibility practices.

use_cases.title: Team Standards Audit
use_cases.description: Run consistent interface reviews across projects without rewriting local review checklists.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Review src/app/page.tsx against the Web Interface Guidelines and list concise findings with file and line references.

prompt_templates.title: Check Component Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all components in src/components for accessibility, spacing, layout, copy, and interaction issues using the current guidelines.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Feature Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changed UI files in this branch against the guidelines. Group findings by severity and include remediation suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review app, component, and design-system files for repeated guideline violations. Identify systemic risks and recommend team-level fixes.

output_examples.input: Review a pricing page for guideline issues.
output: app/pricing/page.tsx:58 - Primary and secondary actions are visually equal. Clarify the main path.
app/pricing/page.tsx:91 - Feature comparison uses color alone. Add text labels for status.

output_examples.input: Audit a component library for interaction quality.
output: components/Dialog.tsx:34 - Focus handling is not described. Verify keyboard entry, escape, and return focus behavior.
components/Card.tsx:76 - Hover-only details may hide information from touch users.

best_practices: Provide the specific files or glob patterns that represent the user flow.
Allow the skill to fetch guidelines only from trusted, reviewed sources.
Ask for severity grouping when the review covers many files.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a whole repository review when only one screen changed.
Do not treat guideline findings as automatic product requirements.
Do not fetch unreviewed guideline sources or paste remote instructions blindly.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews web interface files for design, UX, accessibility, and guideline consistency issues.

faq.question: Does it edit my code?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings unless you separately ask the agent to make changes.

faq.question: Why does it need network access?
faq.answer: It fetches the latest Web Interface Guidelines from the configured source before review.

faq.question: Can I use it in Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it review screenshots?
faq.answer: The skill is written for file-based reviews. Screenshot review would need separate visual context.

faq.question: How should I handle large projects?
faq.answer: Start with changed files or one user flow, then run broader audits after high-impact fixes.
